steps.does: Write the screens, navigation, data model, backend choice and the Android and iOS targets for the agreed scope, as one Expo React Native app.

Build the app as an Expo React Native project whose npm test script runs its tests and whose app.json names the Android package and the iOS bundle identifier; assets are drawn or generated locally, since the sandbox has no network.
Fit every screen to small and large phone sizes, with touch targets, safe areas and the keyboard handled on both platforms.
Cover every screen flow and data rule with tests that fail when the behavior breaks.
Remove dead code, swallowed errors and narration comments behind the tests.

Write the store-ready handover in the brief language: how to run and build each platform, the signing keys and accounts each store needs, the store listing fields, the screenshots to take, the privacy answers and known limits.

steps.ask: The operator builds the signed Android release from app/ (an APK to install and an AAB for Google Play), installs the APK on a phone and checks it against the brief.

When the brief includes iOS, the operator lends his Mac for this step: he builds app/ in Xcode, checks it on a simulator or an iPhone and uploads it to TestFlight under the customer's Apple developer account. Without a Mac the iOS build waits, and the customer is told the new date before the old one passes. When the brief has no iOS app, the step is recorded without files.
The operator checks the data model and the handover notes, then submits to the stores under the customer's developer accounts, which needs the customer's credentials.

acceptance.run: npm install --no-audit --no-fund && npm test && npx expo export --platform android --platform ios --output-dir dist
